title: Your fasting
tomorrow: too many books, one semester. which one does Amira pick?

cards: Four in the afternoon, walking past a dining hall that smells like garlic bread. On a fasting day, every smell turns up its volume. Ramadan's fast is required.
The extra ones aren't. So why would anyone choose one? The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was asked about one of his, and he gave a reason.

teach.b: In Sahih Muslim, someone asks him about fasting on Mondays. He answers: that is the day I was born, and the day revelation came down to me. A voluntary fast can mark what matters.
Other reports name other days: Thursdays, the day of Arafah, the middle days of each lunar month. Now the senses, because the hadith goes there.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, the smell of a fasting person's mouth is better to God than the scent of musk. The thing people apologize for, the stale breath of an empty afternoon, is described as sweeter than perfume. Then taste.

Another report says the fasting person has two joys: one when they break the fast, and one when they meet their Lord. The first joy is completely physical: a date, a glass of water, at sunset after a long day.
And because these fasts are chosen, not owed, they're held more loosely.
A report in Jami' at-Tirmidhi calls the one fasting voluntarily the one in charge of it, free to keep it or break it, though the schools of law differ on whether a broken one should be made up.
One to tell a friend tonight: in the hadith, God prefers the fasting breath to musk.

how: Beyond Ramadan, some Muslims keep voluntary fasts on Mondays and Thursdays, on the middle days of the lunar month, or on days like Arafah, breaking each fast at sunset.

o: the extra fasts you choose beyond Ramadan
a break from social media for one day
skipping one meal a week for your health

games.q: the fast and the senses — tap the pairs.
p: the day he was born, and revelation
the one in charge of it

s: a hadith calls the fasting person's breath better to God than musk
Sahih al-Bukhari: sweeter to God than musk.
the Prophet never gave a reason for his Monday fasts
asked about Mondays, he said: the day I was born, and the day revelation came to me.
voluntary fasts carry exactly the same rules for breaking as Ramadan
a report calls the voluntary faster in charge of the fast; schools differ on making a broken one up.

games.q: your roommate says a voluntary fast is just intermittent fasting with extra steps. she's curious, not mocking. what's the best reply from today?
o: pretty much. it's the same thing, only much older.
it marks what matters, like his Mondays, and the hadith honors even the breath.
it's mostly about proving self-control to yourself.
games.why: he fasted Mondays because of what the day meant, and the hadith turns the hunger's breath and the sunset date into something sacred. a diet doesn't come with two joys.

practice: If there's water nearby, take one sip and hold it in your mouth a moment before swallowing: cold, plain, ordinary. If you're fasting right now, notice your breath instead, and let the sit be part of the waiting.
Either way, stay with how much one ordinary taste can carry.

wordCard.voice: Your fasting: the voluntary fasts you choose beyond Ramadan, like Mondays, Thursdays, or the day of Arafah.

carryVoice: For the road: my fasts, chosen and not owed, with the first joy at sunset. Six of ten, tasted.
